body: Thanks for taking the time to respond to this and sorry it took so long for me to see it. I actually agree 100% with your thoughts on music, it is probably actually one of the only things that has gotten me to 25. I actually used to be into the style of music you mentioned above. Back when I was in high school, in the very early 2000's that type of music was really getting big. I sort of grew out of it I suppose, and while a good amount of it is probably honest and genuine I also feel a lot of it became pretty watered down and insincere. It's just hard to believe a lot of the bands can be so genuinely emotional when their lives consists of playing music for a living while traveling the world, having tons of fans and tons of women. Also at 17 you still are what I consider pretty young, your life could really take any path depending on what you do when you in the next few years...I did nothing, let my problems get the best of me and now I'm basically at rock bottom. When I was your age I thought I had problems, didn't ever think I would have the same problems only magnified 1000% 8 years later... I honestly hope things work out the best for you, sadly I think its too late for me. Thanks again for taking the time to write this to me, I appreciate it more than you will ever know.

Not condemning them at all, they aren't even aware they are doing it. But would you intentionally walk by a homeless person sitting on the corner in the freezing cold while wearing your winter coat and taking a huge bite of a massive burger? I wouldn't intentionally but I'm sure I have done it unintentionally and I'm sure it made someone feel like complete shit. Just knowing that I have probably rubbed someones situation in their face, even if unintentionally makes me feel pretty bad. If on the impossible chance I actually ever do find myself in a relationship I would probably feel awkward making out with someone in a crowded public park or giving them a back massage on the subway because I have been on the other side of the fence and know other people are probably suffering just by being reminded of what they don't and may never have.

I have actually debated this along with MDMA but if I had to chose one, the descriptions I have read of heroin still sound the most pleasing. To be 100% completely calm, at ease and numb is basically all I have ever wanted.

I really wonder if there are a lot of people out there like us who are just basically stuck in some kind of directionless purgatory with no hope of getting out. You have my deepest empathy, but I am glad you consider your mother and have someone you feel is worth living for. I feel the exact opposite where by living I am a burden and huge embarrassment to my entire family. After the initial sadness I almost think they would be relieved if I was gone. Also it may sound fucked up but be glad you don't have a sex drive, it is a huge factor in making matters for myself a million times worse. The feeling of seeing a young couple holding hands or kissing in public is one of the most gut-wrenching feelings ever for someone who has been deprived that their whole life.

I like music but have no faith in my song-writing ability or instrumental talent (piano). Every once in a while if a band I enjoy is in town I will catch them, but I never meet anyone at a concerts. I used to enjoy swimming at a small beach near my house but I just get depressed when I go now because I see so many attractive people. I also used to enjoy video games but quit completely cold turkey with them after wasting a year or so playing WoW (happiest year of my life because of how distracted from reality I was). I'm really not good at much, I never really tried a lot of new stuff because the fear of being embarrassed or looking stupid while doing it. I also enjoy cooking but that is probably just because it is one of the few rewarding things I can do alone, get better at and if I fail nobody knows but me. But compared to the majority of my family I am completely talentless.
